sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 is the downtown business centre of Westfield, drawn at 50 feet to an inch, the only Westfield street sheet at that scale. The sheet is turned slightly, so that North Avenue West runs across the lower part of the page. Elm Street runs up the middle and forks at East Broad Street, which crosses the sheet diagonally from lower left to upper right; Prospect Street and West Broad Street leave it at the lower left, and Quimby Street and Central Avenue branch off to the right. Close-set brick and frame stores with stores, offices and apartments above fill both sides of East Broad Street and Elm Street. They include the Westfield Trust Company bank and the People's Bank, both fireproof, the post office with its lot behind, Moffett and Son, a laundry, drug stores, a printing and telephone exchange building, garages, a moving picture theatre and a hardware and paint store. A brook crosses the block between East Broad Street and the Contractors Yard, and an Italian Roman Catholic church stands at the left edge. Along North Avenue West at the bottom are the North Avenue Hotel, Kelly's Hotel, the Fire Department, garages, an auto laundry and printing works. Below them the Central Railroad of New Jersey runs across the foot of the sheet with its Westbound station and a freight platform. The upper right and left corners are residential and are completed on sheets 3, 4 and 8. A compass and a scale bar in feet are drawn at the right and bottom.
notes: Elm Street, East Broad Street, Prospect Street, Quimby Street, Central Avenue and North Avenue West keep their names today; W. Broad is West Broad Street and E. Broad is East Broad Street.
Westfield Circle (several modern nodes) is not drawn on this sheet; junctions with it were not used.
Lenox Avenue at the right edge was not used as control: its modern junction with Central Avenue lies off the sheet.
50 ft. Downtown: Elm, East and West Broad, Prospect, Quimby, Central Av, North Av W and the Central RR of NJ station; rotation about 11. One part.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 covers a residential district north-west of the Westfield centre, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with the street grid turned about 50 degrees on the page. Prospect Street runs up the page near the right, with Clark Street to the left and Elm Street at the right edge, crossed by Dudley Avenue West and East at the top, Tuttle Parkway and Cowperthwaite Place, Charles Street, Dey Place and Ferris Place, and West Broad Street at the foot. Nelson Place runs between Clark and Prospect Streets. Nearly every lot carries a frame dwelling with a garage; the larger buildings are the brick Roosevelt Public School with its manual training, auditorium and cafeteria wings at the upper left, Westfield Arms Apartments on Prospect Street, the Y.M.C.A. with its gymnasium and swimming pool on Ferris Place, the First M.E. Church, the Town Hall and Fire Department, the American Legion Hall and a florist's greenhouses. At the lower left North Avenue West and South Avenue West run along the Central Railroad of New Jersey, with the tracks and the lumber and coal yards of Tuttle Brothers beside them, and a park with a drive is drawn between the tracks and Ferris Place. A pond is marked in a lot near the top. The compass is drawn in the upper left corner.
notes: Dey Place is Ludlow Place today (modern name from OpenStreetMap).
Clark Street / Cowperthwaite Place / Tuttle Parkway was detected but rejected; the junction is curved on the sheet.
Block 22 on the left lies on sheet 22 and block 19 on sheet 19.
100 ft. North-west of the centre: Dudley Av, Tuttle Pkwy, Prospect, Elm, North and South Av W, West Broad. One part.

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4 shows the north-east part of the Westfield town centre, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with the street grid turned about 50 degrees. Elm Street runs up the left edge, East Broad Street crosses the foot of the sheet, Dudley Avenue East crosses the top and North Euclid Avenue runs up the right edge. Between them Walnut Street, Orchard Street, Kimball Avenue and Cowperthwaite Place run across the page, with Lawrence Avenue and Highland Avenue running up it, and Mountain Avenue cutting diagonally from the lower left to the upper right through a large public park. The park takes the middle of the sheet, with a drive, a brook and two connected lakes. Most lots carry frame dwellings with garages. Institutional buildings are Westfield High School and Washington School, both with their heating and lighting noted, the First Baptist Church, the Presbyterian Church with its Sunday School and parish house, and the post office with stores at the lower left corner. A short strip of dwellings lies along Mountain Avenue at the upper right. The compass is at the lower right.
notes: Mountain Avenue is Mountain Avenue East today.
St. Paul Street is Saint Paul Street today, and Euclid Avenue North is North Euclid Avenue.
100 ft. Mindowaskin Park and lake area, Elm, East Broad, Mountain Av, high school. One part.

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5 covers a residential district of Westfield north-east of the town centre, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with the street grid turned about 50 degrees on the page. East Broad Street closes the sheet at the bottom, Euclid Avenue North runs down the left edge, and North Chestnut Street forms the right edge, with Raymond Street and the Mountain Avenue and Parkview Avenue junction at the top. Between them, Harrison Avenue runs the length of the sheet and is crossed by Kimball Avenue, Maple, Maye and Winyah Avenue. The blocks are numbered 105 to 107, 112, 118, 119, 123 and 124, with the older numbers in parentheses. Almost every lot carries a frame dwelling, many of them with a detached garage. The blocks along Euclid Avenue North and the west side of Harrison Avenue are narrow, deep lots that fan out to the north-west. In the centre of the lower half, Stanley Oval is a loop street with a block numbered (233) inside it, ringed by a few larger houses on irregular lots; a building marked Club Ho. stands south of Maye. The blocks east of Harrison Avenue and south of Maye contain large parcels, many without buildings, and the lower right is largely vacant. At the top left, Mountain Avenue and Raymond Street meet at an acute angle, and the wedge between them is built up with dwellings on radiating lots. Water pipes (6 inch and 12 inch) run in the streets, with hydrants and the fire alarm box at Euclid Avenue and East Broad Street. House numbers appear along every frontage. Sheet 4 adjoins on the left, sheet 6 on the right, sheet 9 below and sheet 26 above.
notes: Printed Raymond is Raymond Street today.
Printed Dudley Avenue East is East Dudley Avenue today; Euclid Avenue North is North Euclid Avenue.
Printed Mountain Avenue in the top left is Mountain Avenue East in OpenStreetMap.
Printed Maple, Maye and Winyah Avenue are Maple Street, Maye Street and Winyah Avenue today; North Chestnut is North Chestnut Street.
Saunders Avenue and Winyah Avenue are lettered along the right edge, where the street lines are drawn but the blocks east of North Chestnut belong to sheet 6.
100 ft. East Broad at the bottom, Euclid Av N left, N Chestnut right; Mountain Av / Raymond at top. One part.

sheet-6.description: Sheet 6 covers the north-eastern edge of built-up Westfield, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with the street grid turned about 50 degrees so that East Broad Street runs across the bottom. North Chestnut runs down the left edge and Oak Avenue across the top; between them the sheet is laid out in a regular grid of long blocks (numbers 149 to 161, with the older numbers in parentheses) cut by Kimball Avenue, Winyah Avenue and Saunders Avenue and by the north-south streets Baker Avenue, Linden Avenue and Jefferson Avenue. Building is confined to the left column of blocks along North Chestnut, where frame dwellings stand on the street frontage, and to a few houses on the frontages of Oak Avenue and of the streets in the bottom left. Most of the interior blocks are drawn as subdivided but vacant strips, with lot lines running across them and no buildings. Jefferson Avenue bends sharply in the upper half, and a strip of narrow lots follows the drawn diagonal boundary of the platted land on the right. East of that line the sheet is open land, numbered 1025 (457) on its large block and left blank except for a compass and the scale bar; a few buildings stand near East Broad Street at the lower right. Garfield Place and a short stretch of Putnam Avenue are drawn at the top right, next to block 161. Water mains (6 inch and 12 inch) run in North Chestnut, Saunders Avenue and East Broad Street, with hydrants at the street corners. Sheet 5 adjoins on the left, sheet 31 above, sheet 32 on the right and below.
notes: Printed North Chestnut is North Chestnut Street today; East Broad is East Broad Street.
Jefferson Avenue is drawn curving in its upper half; the modern line is straight and was not used there.
The lettering along the left edge (Raymond Street, Kimball Avenue, Maple Street, Maye Street) names the cross streets of sheet 5.
The diagonal heavy boundary on the right is the edge of the platted land; the ground beyond is shown on sheet 32.
100 ft. N Chestnut to Jefferson Av, Oak Av to East Broad; mostly vacant platted blocks. One part.

sheet-7.description: Sheet 7 covers the south-western edge of the Westfield centre, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with the grid turned about 40 to 45 degrees. The Central Railroad of New Jersey crosses the upper part from upper left to lower right, with the passenger depot, freight station and ice house beside it, and South Avenue West runs along its south side. Below the railroad the sheet is a residential district of frame dwellings in regular blocks laid out between Westfield Avenue, Summit Avenue, Boulevard and Carleton Road, crossed by 1st Street, Academy Place, Ross Place and Park Street. At the left are Holy Trinity Roman Catholic Church, its school, rectory and Sisters' house, and a small group of houses and a garage on Spring Street. At the upper right North Avenue West and Lenox Avenue meet with an auto repair shop, the Hygier Ice Company and a coal yard, and Central Avenue and New Street at the right edge continue on sheet 8. A park lies between the tracks and the station at the top, with a drive and a triangular island of ground, and West Broad Street enters at the top. The compass is at the upper right, and the scale bar is at the lower left.
notes: Academy Place is Temple Place today (modern name from OpenStreetMap).
Westfield Avenue appears about 30 m east of its drawn position in the modern data near 1st Street; the control point there was placed from the drawn junction.
100 ft. Rail corridor, Westfield Av to Carleton Rd, South Av W, Central Av. Rotation 42-43 (other sheets 50-53); confirmed by an independent fit. One part.

sheet-8.description: Sheet 8 covers the area east of the Westfield centre, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with the grid turned about 50 degrees. East Broad Street crosses the top, Central Avenue runs down the left side and Euclid Avenue South runs up the right. Lenox Avenue, St. Marks Avenue and Tremont Avenue cross the page, with South Elmer Street and curving St. Paul Street between them. The Central Railroad of New Jersey and North Avenue East run diagonally across the lower half, with the lumber and coal yards of J. S. Irving and P. Travnor, a coal elevator and long narrow lots beside the tracks. The blocks above them hold frame dwellings and garages, with the First Congregational Church and parish house, a funeral home, St. Paul's Church, the First Church of Christ, Scientist and its parish house, a public library and a moving picture theatre in the upper left. A brook runs through the block between Lenox Avenue and St. Marks Avenue, and a garage with stores stands where St. Paul Street meets North Avenue East. Lower left blocks along New, Ross Place and Sussex are dwellings. A compass is at the upper left.
notes: Fairmount Avenue is Fairmont Avenue today; St. Marks Avenue is St Marks Avenue; Euclid Avenue South is South Euclid Avenue; Berners Court is not in OpenStreetMap.
100 ft. East of the centre: East Broad to Tremont, Central Av to Euclid Av S; North Av E and the railroad. One part.

sheet-9.description: Sheet 9 covers a residential district of Westfield south-east of the town centre, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with the street grid turned about 45 degrees on the page so that East Broad Street runs across the top. The sheet is bounded by East Broad Street at the top, Hillcrest Avenue at the bottom, South Euclid Avenue on the left and, on the right, South Chestnut Street with a strip of narrow lots along Salter Place and Benson Place beyond it. Between them the regular blocks are cut by Arlington, Lenox, St. Marks, Tremont and Fairmount Avenues, crossed by Archbold Place and Stanley Avenue. Nearly every lot carries a frame dwelling with a frame garage behind it; a few houses are of brick veneer or tile and a handful are drawn in brick. The one institution is Grant Public School, a brick and frame building on the south side of East Broad Street between Archbold Place and Stanley Avenue, with its heating, lighting and construction noted. At the upper right, between East Broad Street, Fair Acres Avenue and Benson Place, a small triangular park is drawn. The far right column of lots along Salter Place is largely undeveloped, with only a few dwellings at its upper end, and the lower right corner is left blank where sheet 33 continues. At the lower left the line of North Avenue East enters the sheet diagonally. Water pipes (6 inch) are drawn in most streets, with fire hydrants and alarm boxes marked at the corners. House numbers are given along every frontage, and block numbers with the older numbers in parentheses.
notes: Fairmount Avenue is spelled Fairmont Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Fair Acres Avenue is Fairacres Avenue today.
The East Broad Street / South Chestnut Street junction was rejected at 15 m: the modern junction no longer sits on the 1928 corner.
Grant Public School on East Broad Street between Archbold Place and Stanley Avenue.
Pilot. 100 ft. South-east residential district: East Broad to Hillcrest, South Euclid to South Chestnut and Salter; Grant Public School. One part.

sheet-10.description: Sheet 10 covers the south-east edge of the built-up part of Westfield, where the Central Railroad of New Jersey (the modern Raritan Valley Line) crosses the sheet diagonally from lower left to upper right as a broad band of tracks. North Avenue East runs along the north-west side of the tracks and South Avenue East along the south-east side. The sheet is drawn at 100 feet to an inch with the street grid turned about 38 degrees from the page. At the left, Hillcrest Avenue and Stanley Avenue bound large, mostly vacant blocks (226, 227, 236, 305) with a pond and a few frame dwellings; 4th Avenue runs from South Chestnut at the top to North Avenue East. North of the tracks, an industrial cluster stands along North Avenue: Knickerbocker Ice Co. and La Bell Cleaners at the top, the Van Doren Laundry Co. in the middle, and Bopf & Whittam Inc. (lanoline manufacturing) at the lower left. A larger plant of the Hermiston corporation and a factory complex stand beside the tracks near the Westfield and Garwood boundary, which crosses the sheet as a dash-dot line marked Town of Westfield and Borough of Garwood. At the right, Garwood's narrow lots front Willow Avenue and Brook. South of the tracks the lower part shows small dwellings on South Avenue East, Livingston, Windsor Avenue, Myrtle Avenue and Grandview Avenue, with the Columbus Public School (built 1926) and blocks 324, 336 and 337. Neighbouring sheets are indicated by the numbers 8, 9, 12, 13, 33, 35, 41 and 52 around the margin.
notes: Carriola Place is Cacciola Place today; Livingston is Livingston Street; South Chestnut is South Chestnut Street.
Euclid Avenue South at the left edge is South Euclid Avenue today; the 'S.' is lettered below the name, so the reading is low confidence.
North Avenue East is drawn about 35 m from the modern line (4th Avenue meets it about 110 ft further south-west than today); it was left out of the georeferencing.
The Hermiston corporation plant is only partly legible at the scan resolution.
The Columbus Public School is marked as built in 1926.
100 ft. South-east edge along the Central RR: North Av E, South Av E, 4th Av, Hillcrest, Columbus Public School. North Av E left out (junctions 12-35 m off). Upper right uncontrolled. One part.

sheet-11.description: Sheet 11 covers a residential district of western Westfield, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with the street grid turned about 50 degrees on the page. Westfield Avenue runs diagonally up the middle of the sheet and Summit Avenue and the Boulevard follow it on the right, crossed by Park at the top, Washington and Everson Place and Beechwood Place lower down. Rahway Avenue cuts down the left side, with Shackmaxon Drive, also lettered Alston Road, running off it towards Westfield Avenue. At the upper left the curving streets Park and Stoneleigh enclose a few large lots, and a brook, drawn in blue, crosses the top-left corner. Almost every lot carries a frame dwelling with a frame garage; a few houses are drawn in brick, and a handful of larger houses stand on the Park and Stoneleigh curves. The blocks along Shackmaxon Drive and Rahway Avenue are cut into deep narrow lots, many still vacant. The one institution is the Lincoln Public School, a large building with its heating, lighting and fire-alarm equipment noted in a legend beside it, standing in a large open block (328) at the lower left between Rahway Avenue and Westfield Avenue. The right half of the sheet is filled by blocks of regular lots with dwellings along their frontages, and several lower blocks on the right are only partly built up. Water pipes of six inches are drawn in most streets, with fire hydrants and alarm boxes at corners. Block numbers 314 to 332 carry the older numbers in parentheses. A compass rose and the scale bar sit in the open space at lower left. The neighbouring sheets are 7 at the top right, 12 at the right, 14 at the bottom, 18 at the left and 19 at the top left.
notes: Shackmaxon Drive is Shackamaxon Drive in OpenStreetMap.
The Boulevard / Washington Street junction was rejected at 6.6 m: the modern node does not sit on the 1928 corner.
Park Street / Summit Avenue has two modern nodes 28 m apart; it was not used as a control point.
100 ft. South-west residential: Boulevard, Summit Av, Westfield Av, Rahway Av, Shackamaxon Dr. One part.

sheet-12.description: Sheet 12 shows a residential district in the south-west of central Westfield, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with the street grid turned about 53 degrees so that Central Avenue runs up the page. The sheet is bounded at the left by Boulevard, at the top by Park and Sussex and at the right by Ripley Place, with Myrtle Avenue and East Grove cutting across the lower right. The left and centre of the sheet are laid out as a curving suburban plan: Carleton Road sweeps from Park down past Washington to Grove, Fairfield Circle encloses an oval block of detached dwellings (block 321), and Midwood Place curves along the lower left. Nearly every lot carries a frame dwelling with a garage, with a few brick houses and a handful of larger buildings drawn in brick or tile. Along the west side of Central Avenue, below Washington, a row of closely spaced buildings drawn in blue stands in block 334. The upper right, between Sussex, Carriola Place and Central Avenue, is the most built-up part, with a continuous run of small stores and dwellings fronting Carriola Place and Sussex and the diagonal South Avenue East crossing the corner. East of Central Avenue the blocks (322, 323, 336, 337, 338) are cut into long narrow lots along Stirling Place, Livingston, Windsor Avenue and Myrtle Avenue, with a machinery storage yard in block 336 and few houses on the Windsor Avenue lots. Water mains of 6 inches run in most streets, and the margin carries the neighbouring sheet numbers 7, 8, 10, 11, 13 and 14.
notes: Carriola Place is Cacciola Place today.
Park is Park Street today, West Grove is Grove Street, East Grove is East Grove Street, Washington is Washington Street, Sussex is Sussex Street, Livingston is Livingston Street.
In the first-pass fit two modern Carleton Road junctions (with Midwood Place and with one of the two Grove Street nodes) were rejected 8 and 21 m from the drawn corners.
100 ft. Boulevard to Ripley Pl, Park to East Grove; Carleton Rd, Fairfield Circle, Central Av. One part.

sheet-13.description: Sheet 13 covers the north-west part of Westfield along the Garwood boundary, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with the street grid turned about 35 degrees counter-clockwise from the page, so that Columbus Avenue runs across the top and Carleton Road along the bottom. The township line between Garwood Borough and Westfield Township is drawn across the top, beyond which blocks are left to the sheet above. The main streets are Columbus, Grandview, Irving, Ripley and Boynton Avenues, which run across the sheet, crossed by Pine, Poplar and Sycamore on the right and by Elizabeth Avenue, which cuts diagonally from the Grandview and Columbus corner down to Central Avenue. At the upper left Myrtle Avenue, Spruce and Locust Avenue meet on the township line in a fan of narrow vacant lots. In the middle right is Pine Circle, a planned crescent of lots round block 354 between Laurel Place and Poplar, mostly vacant. Houses are small frame dwellings with frame garages, concentrated along Columbus and Grandview Avenues and along Central Avenue and Green Place at the lower left. The largest works are those of the Public Service Railway Company at the left, a power and light works with the Westfield car house, a store room and a paint shop. Large parts of blocks 350 to 352, in the lower middle, are open land. A compass rose and the scale bar occupy the lower left and bottom. Water pipes of six inches follow most streets, with fire hydrants and alarm boxes at corners. Blocks 339 to 366 carry their older numbers in parentheses. Neighbouring sheets are 10 on the left, 12 and 14 below, 15 on the right and 41 at the top.
notes: Pine Circle is not in the modern street network used for control.
Carleton Road / Grove Street has two modern nodes about 85 m apart.
Boynton Avenue / Pine Street, Boynton Avenue / Sycamore Street and Central Avenue / Clifton Street were not detected.
100 ft. Central Av to Columbus Av, Myrtle to Carleton Rd; Garwood/Westfield township line. One part.

sheet-14.description: Sheet 14 covers a strip of western Westfield between Carleton Road at the top and Rahway Avenue at the bottom, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with the street grid turned about 37 degrees counter-clockwise from the page, so that the cross streets run across and West Grove runs down the left edge. The streets from the top are Carleton Road, a street lettered Drive beside block 347, the Boulevard, Summit Avenue, Dunham Avenue, Tice Place and Rahway Avenue, all crossed by West Grove on the left, Waite Place in the middle and Clifton on the right. Most of the sheet is laid out in rows of long narrow lots drawn without buildings, an undeveloped subdivision, with houses only near West Grove and in the upper blocks, where frame dwellings and a few brick ones stand along Carleton Road and the Boulevard. At the lower left S. B. McEwen, florist, occupies a large block off West Grove and Westfield Avenue with a potting house, green houses, a furnace room and sheds. Below Tice Place the ground is largely open, with a compass rose and the scale bar in the lower right, and Vermont, Maine and Jersey Streets and Willow Grove Road are only drawn as short stubs running down to Rahway Avenue at the bottom edge. Water pipes of six inches are laid in the developed cross streets. Blocks 341 to 348 carry older numbers in parentheses. Neighbouring sheets are 13 at the top, 12 on the left, 11 at the lower left, 17 on the right and 18 below.
notes: The street lettered Drive beside block 347 is printed with no further name that could be read.
Vermont Street / Rahway Avenue and Willow Grove Road / Rahway Avenue were left out as control: the modern nodes lie 6 to 8 m along Rahway Avenue from the drawn crossings.
Maine Street and Jersey Street are not in the modern street network.
100 ft. Carleton Rd, Summit Av, Dunham Av, Rahway Av. Vermont St and Willow Grove Rd left out (Rahway Av junctions 6-8 m off). One part.

sheet-15.description: Sheet 15 covers the south-western edge of the built-up part of Westfield, between Sycamore at the top and Cedar and Clover Street at the bottom, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with the street grid turned about 53 degrees clockwise from the page, so the main streets run straight up and across it. Boynton Avenue runs down the left of the middle and Central Avenue down the left edge, with Ripley, Irving and Grandview Avenues and Columbus Avenue running down the right half, crossed at the top by Sycamore, in the middle by Center and further down by Fowler and Cedar, with Pearl and Hardwick Avenue as short streets at the left. The blocks between Boynton Avenue and Columbus Avenue, numbered 371 to 379, are plotted in regular lots and are almost entirely undeveloped; only a few houses and outbuildings appear. A single block at the left, 386 and 387 between Pearl and Hardwick Avenue, holds a small group of frame houses, and a long block at the lower left (388) is also open. In the lower middle blocks 389 and 390 are cut into narrow lots along Irving and Welch Avenues. On the right the line between Westfield Township and Garwood Borough is drawn as a dash-dot line, with Cranford Township lettered at the bottom right, and the Garwood blocks beyond hold Hemlock Avenue, Wood Avenue and Center. The upper left corner is filled by the large vacant block 370 and the small side streets Clifton, Midvale and Sunnyside off Central Avenue. The scale bar and a compass rose occupy the foot of the sheet. Neighbouring sheets are 13 at the top, 41 and 40 on the right, 16 below and 17 on the left.
notes: Central Avenue / Clover Street was a 4.6 m residual and was left out of the fit.
Fowler, Welch Avenue, Wood Avenue, Sunnyside Terrace and Landsdowne Avenue are not in the modern street network under these names.
100 ft. Central Av to Columbus Av, Sycamore to Wood Av; Cranford line. Clover St left out. One part.

sheet-16.description: Sheet 16 covers the south-western edge of Westfield, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with the street grid turned about 52 degrees clockwise from the page, so Boynton and Grandview Avenues run down the sheet and the cross streets run across it. Central Avenue is the left boundary, and a township line runs down the right side, with ground beyond it left to Cranford ('See Map of Cranford') and a row of Clark Township lots at the foot of the sheet. The cross streets are Massachusetts, Connecticut, Delaware, Maryland and Virginia, drawn at 50 feet, with the lettered side streets Clover Street, Belmar Terrace, Marlboro Street, Vernon Terrace and Ayliffe Avenue entering from the left. Blocks 388 to 3005 are laid out in regular narrow lots, and the sheet is almost entirely undeveloped: only a few frame dwellings and outbuildings stand on the lots near Boynton Avenue, a farm group with sheds and a poultry house stands in block 395 at the lower left, and a row of seven dwellings lettered A to G, fronting on Picton Avenue, lies inside the Clark Township line at the bottom. Boynton Avenue is marked 80 feet wide and curves at the lower left. A water pipe of six inches is drawn in Central Avenue. The scale bar sits at the lower left and a compass rose at the upper right, with the Sanborn copyright line below the scale bar. Neighbouring sheets are 15 at the top, 17 on the left and Cranford on the right.
notes: Central Avenue / Marlboro Street, Central Avenue / Virginia Street and Central Avenue / Clover Street sat 3.5 to 5.5 m off the other junctions and were left out of the fit.
Picton Avenue, Belmar Terrace and Ayliffe Avenue are not in the modern street network under these names.
The right margin reads 'See Map of Cranford'.
100 ft. Central Av to the Cranford line, Clover St to Virginia (Clark line). Clover St and Marlboro St left out. One part.

sheet-17.description: Sheet 17 covers the southern edge of Westfield at 200 feet to an inch, with the street grid turned about 52 degrees clockwise from the page so that Rahway Avenue runs down the left edge and Summit Avenue down the left of the middle. The sheet is mostly open ground. On the left, a long strip between Rahway Avenue and Summit Avenue holds the large unsubdivided tracts numbered 382, 507, 523 and 528 with only a few farm buildings, labelled Faulkner Farm and Folsom Farm, near Rahway Avenue. To the right of Summit Avenue the Boulevard, Pinegrove and Central Avenue run down the sheet between a block of cross streets, among them Clifton, Midvale Way, Midvale Terrace, Sunnyside Terrace, Landsdowne Avenue, Clover Street (Blvd.), Belmar Terrace, Marlboro, Vernon Terrace and Ayliffe Avenue (Alyff Avenue). The blocks 383A to 385G, with curving streets at the upper middle, are plotted as lots, with only a handful of frame houses along Clifton and Central Avenue and the Westfield Nursery on block 384 at the right. The line between Westfield and Clark Township, with the Lehigh Valley railroad lines beside it, crosses the bottom of the sheet. Summit Street is lettered at the lower left. The scale bar and a compass rose sit at the foot and upper right. Neighbouring sheets are 13 and 14 at the top, 15 and 16 on the right and 41 on the left.
notes: Drawn at 200 feet to an inch; the fit is about 3 m RMSE, so expect metre-level offsets.

The Boulevard and Summit Avenue junctions with Landsdowne Avenue, Midvale Way and Clifton Street sit 15 to 23 m from where the modern streets put them, so they were left out as control and the north end of the sheet rests on the Central Avenue junctions.
Ayliffe Avenue / Summit Avenue and Central Avenue / Clifton Street were not used.
Ayliffe Avenue is lettered with the alternative spelling Alyff Avenue in parentheses.

200 ft. Southern edge: Rahway Av to Central Av, Clark line, Lehigh Valley RR; mostly open (Faulkner and Folsom farms). North third controlled only along Central Av; Landsdowne, Midvale Way, Clifton junctions 15-23 m off and left out. One part.

sheet-18.description: Sheet 18, drawn at 200 feet to an inch, covers a largely undeveloped strip of south-western Westfield along the Fanwood Township line. Lamberts Mill Road runs down the left side with the township line lettered along it, and Rahway Avenue forms the right side, with Stoneleigh Park at the upper right corner. A brook enters at the top right, runs south-west across the sheet and ends in a small pond at the bottom edge. Most of the ground is blank or divided into large numbered blocks (449 to 470), many of them still unplotted farmland. In the upper part a plat of narrow paper streets, Warren, Franklin, William, Charles, Grand, Court and Harrison, is laid out on both sides of Schackamaxon Drive (also lettered Alston Road), with Scotch Plains Avenue South and Hyslip Avenue entering from the top. Almost no buildings stand there. The buildings are concentrated along Rahway Avenue in the upper right, in a cluster of farm buildings with a poultry house near Raritan Road at the lower left, and in the lower right, where small blocks 462 to 469 lie between Pennsylvania, Seward, Baltimore and McKinley Avenues and Vermont, Maine, Jersey and Morgan streets, with a few dwellings along Willow Grove Road. Willow Grove Road crosses the whole width of the sheet about two thirds of the way down. Gardner Avenue and Raritan Road are drawn as unbuilt streets in the lower left. The sheet adjoins sheets 19 and 20 above, 11, 14 and 17 on the right, and 41 below.
notes: Drawn at 200 feet to an inch; the fit gives about 1.95 px/ft.
Schackamaxon Drive and Alston Road, Gardner Avenue, West Grove Street, Court, Grand, Maine, Jersey and Morgan are not in the OpenStreetMap extract.
Warren Street is a paper street on the sheet; the modern Warren Street lies about 40 m east of it, so it was not used.
Only a few street junctions survive in both the sheet and the modern network; the fit leans mainly on Willow Grove Road and Rahway Avenue.
200 ft. Lamberts Mill Rd / Willow Grove Rd / Rahway Av, sparse plat; paper streets (Warren to Charles) not usable. One part.

sheet-19.description: Sheet 19 covers the western residential part of Westfield between Spring and West Broad on the left and Park and Dorian Road on the right, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with the street grid turned about 39 degrees from the page. Rahway Avenue crosses the sheet diagonally from the upper left to the right, and a small brook, drawn in blue, follows it across the middle before turning south-east and leaving at the right edge. At the upper left, South Avenue West, Spring and the first blocks of Rahway Avenue form a cluster of small dwellings and shops (blocks 411, 412, 419). The upper centre and right hold the long blocks between Westfield Avenue and New York Avenue, with detached frame dwellings on deep lots, a Baptist church, and block 306. In the middle, 1st Street, Linwood Avenue, Edgar and Coddington Road bound the long blocks 457A to 457D, which are laid out but only partly built, with a few dwellings on the edges. The McKinley School stands in the left-centre block, and the pink building of Headquarters Troop C, N.G.N.J. (New Jersey National Guard) sits beside the open ground in the middle right. Along the lower left, West Broad and Pierson Street flank blocks 429 and 430, filled with closely set dwellings. At the lower right, Dorian Place, Dorian Court and the curving Dorian Road serve a newly built district. Hyslip Avenue runs along the bottom edge, where sheet 20 continues. Stoneleigh Park is marked at the right edge, and the margin carries the neighbouring sheet numbers 3, 7, 11, 18, 20, 21 and 22.
notes: Spring is probably Watterson Street today; New York Avenue is probably Trinity Place today; Linwood Avenue is Lynwood Place; Coddington Road is Codding Road.
Osborn Avenue South and North are lettered as 'Osborn Av. S.' and 'Osborn Av. N.'; the modern street is Osborn Avenue.
Dorian Place and Dorian Court were left out of the fit: the detected junctions disagreed by 13 to 15 m with where the fit puts the modern nodes.
The 1st Street / Trinity Place junction was left out: it lies about 15 m from the drawn corner.
100 ft. West Westfield: Spring, Rahway Av, Westfield Av, New York Av (now Trinity Pl), Dorian Rd. 1st St / Trinity Pl node and Dorian Pl/Ct left out. One part.

sheet-20.description: Sheet 20 shows the south-western edge of Westfield, from Hyslip Avenue at the top to Lamberts Mill Road at the bottom, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with the street grid turned about 39 degrees from the page. West Broad forms the left edge and Dorian Road the right, and a Fanwood Township line marks the limit of the Westfield plan. The area is a grid of laid-out blocks (431 to 448) crossed by Hazel Avenue, Scotch Plains Avenue South, South Marion Avenue and South Florence Avenue from left to right, and by 1st Street, Austin, Clarence and Warren running down the page. Development is sparse and uneven. The blocks at the upper left and upper right, along Hyslip Avenue, Hazel Avenue and the first block south of it, carry rows of detached frame dwellings with garages, while the central blocks 436 to 438 and most of the area south of Scotch Plains Avenue South are mostly open ground with small clusters of houses on the street frontages. On the right, St. Georges Place, Highgate Place and St. Johns Place cut off short blocks (445 to 448) of new dwellings off Dorian Road, and a column of narrow lots along the far right edge is reached by Charles Street, William Street, Franklin Street and Warren Street. Lamberts Mill Road crosses the lower part as a wide street with a dash-dot line along its lower edge, and the ground south of it is blank except for the lettering Fanwood Township. No schools, churches or works are drawn; a fire alarm box stands at 1st Street and Hazel Avenue. The margin carries the neighbouring sheet numbers 18, 19 and 21.
notes: Coddington Road is Codding Road today; Highgate Place is Highgate Avenue; St. Georges Place is Saint Georges Place; South Marion Avenue and North Marion Avenue are Marion Avenue and North Marion Avenue; South Florence Avenue is Florence Avenue; Scotch Plains Avenue South is Scotch Plains Avenue; Scotch Plains Avenue North is North Scotch Plains Avenue.
Pierson Street, Edgar Road and Coddington Road are lettered at the top edge only, where they continue from sheet 19.
Suffixes of the longer street labels (Place, Avenue) were read at reduced width and are medium confidence.
100 ft. South-west edge: Hyslip Av to Lamberts Mill Rd, mostly vacant laid-out blocks, Fanwood line. One part.

sheet-21.description: Sheet 21 lies on the western edge of Westfield, where the town meets Fanwood Township, and is drawn at 100 feet to an inch with the street grid turned about 52 degrees on the page. A dash-dot township line runs diagonally from the lower left to the top, and the large area to its left, labelled Fanwood Township, is a laid-out but almost empty grid of blocks (473 to 485) with Adams, Hancock, Cumberland, North Marion Avenue and North Florence Avenue ruled across it and only two houses at the bottom corner. The built part of the sheet is the strip on the right between Scotch Plains Avenue North and Palsted Avenue: blocks 422 to 426 have detached frame dwellings on narrow lots facing Drake Place, Roosevelt, Hort (Walnut), Cumberland and Downer, with block 479 to their left empty. At the top, small lots in blocks 428 and 441 front Newark Avenue, Graceland Place and Elizabeth Avenue, and at the upper right South Avenue W. runs diagonally beside a large block (427) of narrow lots and the corner of the Central Railroad of New Jersey tracks, with Crossway Place at the head of the sheet. West Broad lies along the foot of the sheet, where sheet 20 continues and where the lettering of South Florence Avenue, South Marion Avenue, Scotch Plains Avenue South and Hyslip Avenue begins. No schools, churches or industrial works are drawn. The margin carries the neighbouring sheet numbers 19, 20, 22 and 23.
notes: Hort (Walnut) is Hort Street today; Roosevelt is Roosevelt Street; Cumberland is Cumberland Street; Downer is Downer Street; Hancock is Hancock Street; Scotch Plains Avenue North is North Scotch Plains Avenue.
Adams and the Fanwood Township blocks (473 to 485) have no matching streets in the OpenStreetMap extract and were not used for control.
The junction of South Avenue West, Crossway Place and North Scotch Plains Avenue at the top was left out of the fit because it measured 4.7 m from the other points.
The suffixes of the labels at the foot of the sheet (South Florence Avenue, South Marion Avenue, Scotch Plains Avenue South, Hyslip Avenue) are partly cut by the sheet edge and are medium confidence.
100 ft. West edge at the Fanwood line; Palsted Av to Scotch Plains Av N strip built. Three-way Y at the top excluded. One part.

sheet-22.description: Sheet 22 shows the western approach to the centre of Westfield, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with the street grid turned about 52 degrees on the page. The wide band of the Central Railroad of New Jersey tracks (the modern Raritan Valley Line) crosses the sheet diagonally from the upper left to the lower right, with North Avenue West running along its north-east side and South Avenue West along its south-west side. South-west of the railroad, a regular grid of blocks (413 to 417, 421, 422) lies between Palsted Avenue on the left and Osborn Avenue North on the right, cut by Hort (Walnut), Cumberland and Downer and closed at the foot by West Broad. These blocks are lined with detached frame dwellings on narrow lots, a church stands near Osborn Avenue North and Cumberland, and the lower right corner, where Osborn Avenue North meets the railroad, holds a group of larger buildings drawn in yellow and a small blue-and-pink cluster, evidently an industrial yard. At the left, triangular blocks 416 and 417 are cut off by the diagonal of South Avenue West, with Roosevelt and Drake Place at the left margin. North-east of the tracks the diagonal blocks (404, 408, 409) front North Avenue West and Osborn Avenue North, and the curve of Tuttle Parkway leads at the top to the fan-shaped lots of block 113A, with the junction of Coleman Place and Dudley Avenue West at the top edge and Charles at the right. A large vacant area at the right is marked 113, 113B and 3. The margin carries the neighbouring sheet numbers 3, 19, 21, 23 and 24.
notes: Hort (Walnut) is Hort Street today; Dudley Avenue West is West Dudley Avenue; Roosevelt is Roosevelt Street; Cumberland and Downer are Cumberland Street and Downer Street; Osborn Avenue North is Osborn Avenue; Charles is Charles Street.
Tuttle Parkway is lettered 'Tuttle Pkwy.' on the sheet.
North Avenue West, South Avenue West and Tuttle Parkway are drawn as diagonals beside the railroad; the drawn railroad lies within about 4 m of the modern Raritan Valley Line.
100 ft. Central RR diagonal, North Av W / South Av W, Tuttle Pkwy, blocks 413-422. One part.

sheet-23-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 23 covers the western edge of Westfield where it meets Fanwood Township, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with the street grid turned about 52 degrees on the page. It runs from Seneca Place at the top down to Dudley Avenue West and the Central Railroad of New Jersey at the bottom, and from the Fanwood Township line on the left to Coleman Place on the right. The upper right holds block 176 along Forest Avenue and Eaglecroft Road, and a row of houses on the south side of Seneca Place, several marked as drawn from plans. A wedge of unbuilt lots on the left, blocks 1020 to 1022 in Fanwood Township, is cut by Longfellow, Bryant, Channing and Whittier Avenues and bounded by Florence. Most of the middle of the sheet is the large vacant block 168. Along Coleman Place and Holmes Place there are frame dwellings, with Edgewood Parkway, a divided street with a planted median, between Holmes Place and Coleman Place. The lower half is the more built-up: Birch Place and block 168A with a row of dwellings with fireproof concrete garages, and the frontage of Dudley Avenue West. At the lower left North Avenue West and the four-track railroad cross the sheet diagonally; between them stand the gasometer (125 ft, 750,000 cubic feet) and buildings of the Elizabethtown Consolidated Gas Co., and south of the tracks the Freeman Saw Mill, marked not in operation, beside Crossway and South Avenue West. Scotch Plains Avenue North and Elizabeth Avenue are lettered at the lower left edge. A heavy line at the upper left sets off part 2, an inset of the ground north of Seneca Place.
notes: Florence (the street bounding the wedge of blocks 1020 to 1022) is today's Poets Place; Poets Place / Whittier Avenue fitted at 0.6 m.
Edgewood Parkway is Edgewood Avenue today; the Coleman Place / Edgewood Avenue node was rejected at 9.6 m (the parkway is drawn as two roadways).
Holmes Place is not in OpenStreetMap.
Longfellow and Channing Avenues now run through to Forest Avenue across the 1928 block 168; those junctions are not drawn and were excluded.
Elizabethtown Consolidated Gas Co. gasometer and works on North Avenue West; Freeman Saw Mill, not in operation, at Crossway.
The drawn railroad lies about 11 m from the modern Raritan Valley Line against the street fit.

100 ft. Two parts: part 1 main (Seneca Pl to Dudley Av W and South Av W, Coleman Pl to the Fanwood line; gas works, railroad); part 2 inset at upper left behind a heavy line (Ohio, Hill, South St, Graceland Av and Rd, north side of Seneca Pl, Fanwood Township), ground just north of part 1, not placed.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Ohio, Hill, South St, Graceland Av and Rd north of Seneca Place (Fanwood Township) (streets replatted (modern Forest Avenue curve, Tuttle Parkway); no surviving junction found; needs carried points from sheet-23-1 along Seneca Place, or parcel corners on the north side of Seneca Place).

sheet-24.description: Sheet 24 shows a residential district in western Westfield, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with the street grid turned about 50 degrees on the page. Coleman Place bounds it on the left, Seneca Avenue and Effingham Place on the top, Prospect on the right and Dudley Avenue West, with Tuttle Parkway, along the bottom. Eaglecroft Road, Edgewood Avenue and Stanmore Place cross it from side to side, and Hanford Place, Embree Crescent and Clark run across them. Embree Crescent curves through the middle, its upper arm drawn as a diagonal street cutting through block 179, and encloses block 135 with a large brick dwelling and the sheet's north arrow. At the right, Lincoln Road loops around block 136A and Webster Place meets Lincoln Road. Edgewood Parkway at the lower left is drawn as two roadways either side of a narrow central strip. Nearly every lot carries a frame dwelling, shown in yellow, with a frame garage behind; a few houses are brick or tile (pink) and one or two are stone (blue). The upper middle, between Seneca Avenue and the Embree Crescent diagonal, is more sparsely built, with long lots and unbuilt frontage. Six-inch water pipes run in most streets and a twelve-inch main along Dudley Avenue West, with fire hydrants, telephone boxes and a fire alarm at several corners. House numbers are given along the frontages. The sheet adjoins sheets 23 on the left, 22 and 3 below, 25 on the right and 27 above.
notes: Seneca Avenue is Seneca Place in OpenStreetMap.
Hanford Place and Coleman Place keep their names today.
The junction of Embree Crescent and Seneca Place was left out of the fit: the modern node lies 4 to 5 m from the drawn corner.
The junction of Coleman Place and Edgewood Avenue was left out: Edgewood Parkway is drawn as two roadways and the modern node is about 10 m off.
100 ft. Embree Crescent / Clark / Edgewood district. One part.

sheet-25.description: Sheet 25 covers the area between Prospect and Highland Avenue in western Westfield, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned about 50 degrees on the page. Prospect runs down the left side and Highland Avenue down the right, with Lawrence Avenue running parallel between them and then angling off to the upper right. Elm lies between Prospect and Lawrence Avenue. Newton Place and Sinclair Place cross the sheet from side to side in its upper third, Sylvania Place curves through the centre between Elm and Lawrence Avenue, and Dudley Avenue East closes the bottom with Dudley Avenue West at the lower left. At the left edge Effingham Place, Stanmore Place and Lincoln Road enter from sheet 24. The upper half of the middle is a single large unplotted block, 137 (351), showing only the north arrow, with a strip of lots along Prospect on its left that includes a florist's greenhouses. Below Newton Place the lots are narrow and mostly built with frame dwellings and garages (yellow), with a few brick or tile houses (pink). The blocks between Lawrence Avenue and Highland Avenue (133 and 138) are similarly built, while the upper right, along Highland Avenue, Birch Avenue and Colonial Avenue, has only scattered houses on large lots. A fire alarm box stands at Lawrence Avenue and Sinclair Place. Six-inch water pipes run in the streets and a twelve-inch main in Dudley Avenue. The sheet adjoins sheets 24 on the left, 28 and 30 above, 26 on the right, and 3 and 4 below.
notes: Alden Avenue, printed at the right edge, is Alden Street in OpenStreetMap.
Elm Street and Newton Place keep their names today.
The junction of Elm and Newton Place was not detected; the fit rests on twelve junctions, mostly along Prospect, Elm, Lawrence Avenue and Highland Avenue.
100 ft. Prospect to Highland Av, Sylvania Pl. One part.

sheet-26.description: Sheet 26 shows the dense residential district north-east of Westfield's centre, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned about 50 degrees on the page. Highland Avenue bounds it at the left, Dudley Avenue East at the lower left, and North Chestnut at the right, with Bradford Avenue curving across the top. Its distinguishing feature is a group of diagonal streets, Mountain Avenue, Standish Avenue, Alden Avenue and Colonial Avenue, running at an angle to the main grid and meeting at several irregular junctions. Mountain Avenue runs from the lower centre up to Standish Avenue at the upper right, where Priscilla Lane, Cedar Terrace and Belvidere Avenue lead off. Birch Avenue and Colonial Avenue curve from Bradford Avenue to the diagonal streets. At the lower right Parkview, Raymond, Cory Place and Oak Avenue bound blocks 126, 127 and 128. Blocks 134, 134A and 140 to 147B are lined with frame dwellings and garages (yellow), with a number of brick or tile houses (pink) and a few stone buildings (blue), including a large building at the upper left in block 140. The lots in the diagonal blocks are narrow and run perpendicular to the diagonal streets. Six-inch water pipes run in the streets, twelve-inch mains in Dudley Avenue East and North Chestnut, with hydrants and one fire alarm box at Mountain Avenue. The sheet adjoins sheets 25 on the left, 30 above, 31 on the right, 4 below and 6 and 5 at the bottom right.
notes: Alden Avenue is Alden Street in OpenStreetMap; Cedar Avenue is lettered in parentheses on the same diagonal street as an earlier name.
Priscilla and the separate label La. above it are read together as Priscilla Lane.
The label Parkview on the diagonal street and a separate Av. on the street running to North Chestnut may be one name; read as Parkview, low confidence.
Mountain Avenue is Mountain Avenue East today, and North Chestnut is North Chestnut Street.
100 ft. Highland Av to N Chestnut, Mountain / Standish diagonals. One part.

sheet-27.description: Sheet 27 covers the north-western corner of the Westfield survey, along the Fanwood Township line, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned about 50 degrees on the page. The township line crosses the upper left as a dash-dot line. West of Fanwood Avenue lies an old subdivision of very long narrow lots, blocks 185 to 189 and 188A, between North Everts Avenue, Cleveland Avenue, John Avenue, Brown Avenue and Fanwood Avenue, with a diagonal Brightwood Avenue cutting across their lower ends. Few of those lots are built. Brightwood Avenue turns at Embree Crescent and runs straight across the sheet to Prospect on the right. The upper right is dominated by a vast unplotted block, 191 (319), with the north arrow, bounded on the north by Pleasant Avenue and Smith, where Randolph Place and Clinton Place enter from sheet 29, and a few small lots lie along Prospect. At the lower left Graceland Road runs diagonally past block 184 (338) and a triangular lot with dwellings, and Seneca Place runs along the bottom edge with a row of houses. Below Brightwood Avenue blocks 179, 181 and 182 hold frame dwellings and garages, with Clark and Embree Crescent running north and Effingham Place at the bottom. Six-inch water pipes are shown in the streets and hydrants and a fire alarm box at Clark and Effingham Place. The sheet adjoins sheets 29 above, 23 on the left, 24 below and 28 on the right.
notes: Fanwood Avenue and Brightwood Avenue keep their names today; the modern Fanwood Avenue runs north-west from Brightwood Avenue.
John Avenue is John Street in OpenStreetMap, and North Everts Avenue is Everts Avenue.

Much of the upper left subdivision (Cleveland, John, Brown) does not follow the modern street lines exactly; Smith, Pleasant Avenue, Randolph Place and Clinton Place are not in the OpenStreetMap extract and were not used.
The junction of Embree Crescent and Seneca Place was left out of the fit: the modern node lies about 4 m from the drawn corner.
100 ft. Fanwood line, Brightwood Av, Embree Crescent. One part.

sheet-28.description: Sheet 28 covers a mostly unbuilt subdivision between Prospect and the long line of Lawrence Avenue in north-western Westfield, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned about 50 degrees on the page. Prospect runs down the left edge. A grid of paper streets, Washington Avenue, Lexington Avenue, Lafayette Avenue and Berkley Terrace across, with Carteret and Sedgwick Avenue down, cuts a block of very narrow lots, numbered 192 to 199 (323 to 329). Only a handful of dwellings and sheds have been built, mainly along Washington Avenue, in blocks 193 and 198 and at the lower left. A broad vacant strip lower down is marked Brightwood Avenue, Proposed, as two dashed lines running across to Lawrence Avenue, where Hillside Avenue is a stub on the east side. At the lower left a row of lots along Prospect holds a few frame dwellings and sheds, and Effingham Place enters from the left edge. The right half of the sheet is open ground in blocks 148 (322) and 137 (351), crossed by Lawrence Avenue, a long straight street 66 feet wide with a frame dwelling and outbuilding near its middle, and by irregular property lines. The compass and north arrow stand in the upper middle. The sheet adjoins sheets 29 above, 27 on the left, 30 on the right and 25 below. Six-inch water pipes are drawn along Prospect.
notes: Carteret is lettered Carteret (Elm) on its lower stretch, so Elm is an earlier name.
Brightwood Avenue is marked Proposed across the lower part and is drawn as dashed lines.

The paper streets Washington Avenue, Lexington Avenue, Lafayette Avenue, Berkley Terrace, Carteret and Sedgwick Avenue are not in OpenStreetMap; Washington Avenue appears to be Hamilton Avenue and Berkley Terrace Sedgewick Court at their junctions with Prospect.
Only Prospect and Lawrence Avenue junctions are available, so the fit is weak across the sheet.
100 ft. Prospect to Lawrence Av, paper-street subdivision; 4 of 5 points on Prospect: low confidence. Washington Av = Hamilton Av and Berkley Ter = Sedgewick Ct (by position). One part.

sheet-29.description: Sheet 29 covers the western edge of Westfield where it meets Fanwood Township, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with the street grid turned about 38 degrees to the left on the page. Prospect crosses the sheet from left to right at about the middle, and above it Caldwell Avenue and Sedgwick Avenue cut the long, narrow lots of blocks 1001, 1009, 1010, 1012 and 1013 on either side of Madison Avenue East and Sherman Avenue East. Below Prospect the sheet is a grid of blocks 1007, 1008, 1011 (302), 1004 to 1006 and 1003 (306), laid out along Sherman Avenue West, Madison Avenue West, Liberty, North Marlborough Street, South Marlborough Street and Netherwood Avenue, with Marlborough Place, Marlborough Road, Clinton Place and Randolph Place as cross streets and Smith on the right edge. A strip of closely platted lots lies along the bottom, facing Fanwood Avenue. Dwellings are scattered: a group of frame houses stands along Madison Avenue West, the Madison Avenue Methodist Chapel is lettered near Overhill, and a school and a church stand on the right. Most lots, especially in the upper blocks and between Marlborough Road and Netherwood Avenue, are vacant. The township line crosses the lower left diagonally and Fanwood Township is lettered across the bare ground south-west of it. At the left, Overhill and Brisbane Place serve blocks 1014 (301), 1023 and 1024. Sheet 30 adjoins above and at the left, sheet 28 on the right and sheet 27 at the lower right.
notes: Only Madison Avenue, Prospect Street, Liberty Street and Fanwood Avenue are in the OpenStreetMap extract; Sherman, Marlborough, Netherwood, Clinton, Randolph and Caldwell are not, and this part of Westfield has been replatted.
Printed Prospect is Prospect Street today; Liberty is Liberty Street; Overhill is Overhill Street; Smith is Smith Street.
Printed Sedgwick Avenue differs from the modern Sedgewick Avenue, which lies about 130 ft south of where the sheet draws it.
The part rests on two junctions (Madison Avenue and Prospect Street, Liberty Street and Fanwood Avenue) fitted as a helmert; the fitted scale and rotation agree with the atlas.
Some labels at the right edge (Netherwood Avenue, Smith, Clinton Place, Randolph Place) were read on lower-resolution crops.
100 ft. Fanwood Township edge (Madison, Sherman, Marlborough, Netherwood); helmert on two junctions: low confidence. One part.

sheet-30-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 30 covers the north-western corner of Westfield along the Mountainside line, drawn at 200 feet to an inch with the grid turned about 51 degrees on the page. Most of the sheet is open land: Lawrence Avenue runs the full height of the page from Hillside Avenue up to the Mountainside Borough boundary, which crosses the upper part of the sheet as a dash-dot township line, and the large tracts on either side of it (block 148 to the west, block 173 to the east) hold only a handful of dwellings and outbuildings. Several township lines cross the eastern half of the sheet. Along the left edge the ends of streets on the adjoining sheet 29 are lettered: Sherman Avenue East, Madison Avenue East and Caldwell Avenue at the top, then Washington Avenue, Lexington Avenue, Lafayette Avenue and Berkley Terrace. The built-up part is the bottom strip along Hillside Avenue: frame dwellings on Hillside Avenue and on the curving Highland Avenue and Bradford Avenue, and at the lower right a small subdivision with Cedar Terrace, Priscilla Lane, Mountain View Circle and Standish Avenue, where blocks 147 and 147B to 147E are laid out and partly built, some houses marked as drawn from plans. Mountain View Terrace is lettered at the lower right corner. A heavy line from the top edge to the right edge sets off part 2, which shows ground near Prospect Street, Springfield Road and the Mountainside and Fanwood lines and is drawn displaced on the page.
notes: Mountain View Circle and Mountain View Terrace are Mountainview Circle and Mountainview Terrace in OpenStreetMap.
Control is all along Hillside Avenue at the bottom of the sheet (6 points); the upper three quarters, mostly open land, has no control: low confidence there.
Bradford Avenue / Cedar Terrace was rejected at 8.2 m.

200 ft. Two parts: part 1 main (Lawrence Av, Hillside Av, Cedar Ter subdivision; mostly open land up to the Mountainside line); part 2 upper right behind a heavy line (Prospect St, Springfield Rd, Sherman Av E, Caldwell Av, Madison Av E, Overhill), displaced, not placed.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Prospect Street, Springfield Road, Sherman Avenue East, Caldwell Avenue near the Mountainside and Fanwood lines (Sherman Av E, Caldwell Av, Overhill and Springfield Rd not identified in OpenStreetMap (Springfield Rd probably US 22); no usable junction; needs identification of the streets and hand-picked or parcel-corner control).

sheet-31.description: Sheet 31 shows the northern edge of Westfield at its boundary with Mountainside Borough, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with the street grid turned about 38 degrees to the left of vertical. North Chestnut runs along the bottom, the Oak Avenue line along the right edge, and Woodland Avenue crosses the upper left diagonally from Mountain Avenue towards the north-east. The best-developed ground is the block bounded by Garfield Avenue, Grant Avenue, Girard Avenue and Lincoln Avenue (block 165) and the block east of it (164), laid out with dashed 6 inch water pipes on their edges; most lots in them are vacant, with a scattering of frame dwellings and a pair of coops. Along the lower half, Belvidere Avenue and Sherwood Parkway serve a column of houses between Terrace Place and North Chestnut, and a second column of frame dwellings stands along the bottom edge on North Chestnut and Park View Avenue. The upper left carries long narrow lots on both sides of Woodland Avenue in Mountainside Borough, among them blocks 1026 and (356), with houses strung along the avenue. At the left edge Mountain Avenue meets New Providence Road, where a small group of pink-coloured tile-roofed dwellings stands, and Mountain View Terrace, Priscilla Lane and Standish Avenue appear at the lower left in block 147E. The dash-dot township line runs diagonally across the sheet and then west along the left side, separating Westfield from Mountainside. A private road, Hamilton's Crossway, crosses the middle. The large central tract between it and Terrace Place is open ground. Sheet 30 adjoins at the lower left, sheet 32 at the top and right and sheet 6 at the lower right.
notes: Printed Lincoln Avenue (between Grant and Franklin Avenues) is Wallberg Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Printed Park View Avenue is Parkview Avenue today; North Chestnut is North Chestnut Street; Mountain View Terrace is Mountainview Terrace.
Hamilton's Crossway is lettered Private and has no modern counterpart in OpenStreetMap.
Sherwood Parkway is drawn curving at its east end; its junctions fit worse than the straight street junctions and Belvidere Avenue and Sherwood Parkway carries the largest residual.
Franklin Avenue is drawn about 34 ft wide, narrower than the 51 ft right-of-way today.
100 ft. Woodland Av, Mountainside line, Garfield/Grant/Girard, Belvidere/Sherwood. Lincoln Av = Wallberg Av. One part.

sheet-32.description: Sheet 32 is the outlying sheet of the Westfield atlas, drawn at 400 feet to an inch, and shows the sparsely settled ground north-east of the town where Westfield, Mountainside Borough, Springfield Township and Cranford Township meet. East Broad runs north from the small built-up cluster at the bottom of the sheet, where Linden, Baker, Fair Acres, Arlington and Lenox streets are laid out in blocks 237 (460) and 238 (461), up past Woodland Avenue and Gallows Hill Road to Springfield Avenue, which crosses the upper centre. Westfield's boundary with Mountainside Borough runs along the left, enclosing Echo Lake, a long narrow pond with the Echo Lake Country Club on its east shore and Nassau Road along its north-west side. The township line to the east is marked by a dash-dot line, and the strip beyond it is labelled as continuing on the map of Cranford Township. Most of the sheet is large unsubdivided tracts (blocks 247 (458), 248 (454), 1025 (457), 1026 (453)) with scattered dwellings strung along Springfield Avenue, East Broad, Woodland Avenue and Nassau Road. At the lower left the streets of sheets 31 and 6 appear in miniature: Garfield, Franklin, Putnam, Oak and Jefferson, with Saunders, Linden and Baker, and Kimball further right. At the lower right Benson Place and Salter Street run east out of the cluster towards sheet 33. A compass at the upper left carries the sheet's north. Sheets 31, 6 and 9 adjoin below, sheet 33 and 34 on the right.
notes: Printed East Broad is East Broad Street today; Fair Acres Avenue is Fairacres Avenue.
Nassau Road, Garfield Place and Salter Street are not in the OpenStreetMap extract; Salter Place is the nearest modern name.

At 400 ft to an inch this sheet is a compiled overview, not a surveyed plan: the six hand-picked junctions fit only to about 14 m RMSE (leave-one-out 20 m), and the East Broad junctions disagree with the lower left cluster by up to 30 m, so the placement is approximate.
Several street names in the lower left cluster (Kimball, Franklin, Putnam, Oak, Jefferson) were read on crops at lower resolution than the other sheets.
400 ft. Echo Lake, Springfield Av, East Broad north, Gallows Hill Rd; 6 hand picks, RMSE 14 m; second_pass keep. Approximate. One part.

sheet-33.description: Sheet 33 straddles the boundary between Westfield and the Borough of Garwood, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. The Garwood half, in the lower right, is drawn with north near the top: a grid of blocks 43 to 47 between 4th Avenue, 3rd Avenue, 2nd Avenue and North Avenue, bounded on the right by Walnut and crossed by Maple. Its blocks hold closely built frame dwellings, with three public schools in block 43: Franklin School, Jefferson School and Lincoln School, the last with a gymnasium and auditorium of cinder block walls. The lower right block also holds Britz Park, with a hall and the Britz Hotel, and a greenhouse. At the lower left, block 35 is the works of Henry B. Newhall Corpn and the Diamond Expansion Bolt Co., hardware makers, with sprinklers and watchman's clock noted. The Westfield half, at the upper left, is turned about 50 degrees on the page. Salter, Benson Place and South Chestnut run diagonally, with large undeveloped blocks (229, 230, 231, 232) and a few houses on Salter. Stevens Avenue and Cranford Avenue cross the upper centre between long platted blocks (239, 240, 242) of narrow lots, nearly all vacant. A dash-dot line, the boundary of Westfield Township and Garwood Borough, runs diagonally across the sheet and then turns east along the top of the Garwood blocks. The upper right shows the blank end of sheet 34 with Sherman, Morris Avenue, Union and Essex Avenue. Sheets 9 and 10 adjoin at the left, sheet 32 above, sheet 34 at the right and sheets 35 and 36 below.
notes: Printed Maple is Maple Avenue today; Walnut is Walnut Street; Union Street and Union are Union Street.
Printed South Chestnut is South Chestnut Street; Sherman is Sherman Street.
Essex Avenue is not in OpenStreetMap.
The fit excludes the 4th Avenue junctions with Walnut and with Union Street, which sit 4 m off the modern streets where 4th Avenue bends.

The Garwood grid is drawn with north near the top while the Westfield streets (Salter, Benson Place, Stevens and Cranford Avenues) lie at about 50 degrees to it; one transformation (rotation about 10 degrees) fits both.
100 ft. Salter, Benson, Stevens, Cranford Avs (Westfield) and Garwood north of North Av (Maple, Walnut; Franklin, Jefferson and Lincoln schools). One part.

sheet-34-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 34 covers the north side of central Garwood, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north close to the top of the page. It runs from North Avenue at the bottom up through 2nd, 3rd and 4th Avenues to 5th Avenue, and from Walnut and Union on the left to Oak Street North on the right, with Cedar crossing the middle. The North Avenue frontage between Walnut and Cedar is the business end of the sheet: a hotel at the Walnut corner, a brick public garage (capacity 30 cars), brick bowling alleys, a block of stores with a post office and a bakery, dwellings with stores, and the brick Church of St. Anne (Roman Catholic) set back from the avenue. A second hotel stands on North Avenue east of Cedar. Between 2nd and 4th Avenues west of Cedar lie two large irregular blocks (75 and 75A) crossed diagonally by Old Road, with a few dwellings and sheds. East of Cedar the blocks between North Avenue and 4th Avenue are fully divided into narrow lots with frame dwellings and garages, and block 49 above 4th Avenue reaches to 5th Avenue. At the upper left, beyond the borough line marked Town of Westfield and Borough of Garwood, the blocks along Morris Avenue, Union, Sherman and Essex Avenue belong to Westfield, and Brookside Place runs off 4th Avenue near the boundary. Much of the upper half is blank and lettered Cranford Township, See Map of Cranford, behind a heavy line that frames part 2, an inset of the blocks along Stevens, Cranford and Morris Avenues. Fire alarm boxes, hydrants and 6 and 12 inch water pipes are marked.
notes: Walnut is Walnut Street, Cedar is Cedar Street and Oak Street North is North Oak Street in OpenStreetMap.
Essex Avenue is not in OpenStreetMap.
Church of St. Anne (Roman Catholic), bowling alleys, a public garage, a post office and two hotels on North Avenue.

100 ft. Garwood north of North Av (Walnut to Oak St N, North to 5th Av) with Westfield blocks at upper left (Morris Av, Union, Sherman, Essex Av). Two parts: part 1 main; part 2 V-shaped inset (Stevens, Cranford, Morris Avs north-west of Sherman), placed by a helmert on three Sherman St junctions.

sheet-34-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 34 is an inset in the upper middle of the sheet, framed by a heavy V-shaped line, showing an undeveloped subdivision on the Westfield side of the Garwood line north-west of Sherman. It is drawn at the same scale as the main map, 100 feet to an inch, and at nearly the same orientation, but displaced on the page: on the ground it lies beyond the upper left corner of part 1, continuing the blocks along Morris Avenue and Sherman. Three parallel streets, Stevens Avenue, Cranford Avenue and Morris Avenue, run north-east from Sherman, which crosses the lower end of the inset. They bound blocks 238, 241 and 243 (old numbers 461, 463 and 464 in parentheses), which are divided into rows of narrow lots, with 40 ft lots at the Sherman end. The blocks are almost entirely vacant; the only building is a single frame dwelling on the north side of Morris Avenue. Sheet numbers 32, 33 and 34 printed in the inset give the adjoining sheets. The right-hand side of the inset is blank, lettered Cranford Township and See Map of Cranford, with the borough line drawn as a dash-dot line, and the north arrow of the sheet stands in this blank area.
notes: Placed from three detected junctions on Sherman Street (Stevens, Cranford, Morris), all along one street: helmert, low confidence.
Sherman is Sherman Street in OpenStreetMap.

100 ft. Garwood north of North Av (Walnut to Oak St N, North to 5th Av) with Westfield blocks at upper left (Morris Av, Union, Sherman, Essex Av). Two parts: part 1 main; part 2 V-shaped inset (Stevens, Cranford, Morris Avs north-west of Sherman), placed by a helmert on three Sherman St junctions.

sheet-35.description: Sheet 35 shows the north-western end of the Garwood industrial belt, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the right of the page. Willow Avenue runs down the left edge and South Avenue parallels it a short distance to the right, with Maple crossing both near the lower left. The ground between them is divided into narrow lots, most of them vacant, with a scatter of frame dwellings and sheds. East of South Avenue the sheet is given to factories. A long building of the Brass & Copper Tube Works Inc., marked not in operation, fronts the avenue, with Vendex Inc., maker of vending machines, and a paint shop beside it. Lower down a large vacant factory stands beside a plant making washing powder, and the Rodic Rubber Co., rubber goods manufacturers, occupies a long block farther south. At the foot of the sheet are the works of the Esda Mfg. Co. Inc., makers of water heaters, which continue onto sheet 36. To the right a broad band of parallel railroad tracks and sidings crosses the sheet from top to bottom; a freight house lies beside it and the name Garwood is lettered at the tracks. The Hudson Fireproof Brick Co., a cement block works with drying kilns and a shed, stands beyond the tracks at the upper right. North Avenue runs down the right edge, with South Chestnut Street entering it from the right near the foot of the sheet. A diagonal line lettered Town of Westfield and Borough of Garwood marks the boundary at the upper right. Water pipes, hydrants and fire alarm boxes are marked in the streets.
notes: South Avenue, Maple, North Avenue, Willow Avenue and Chestnut Street (printed South Chestnut Street) are named as the same streets in OpenStreetMap; Maple is Maple Avenue.
The sheet is turned: north is about 11 degrees from the right-hand edge, so streets that run east and west today run up and down the page.
Only three junctions were used (Maple with Willow Avenue and South Avenue, and North Avenue with Chestnut Street).
50 ft. Garwood factory belt, Willow Av to North Av at Maple; turned (north to the right). Exact 3-point fit with one hand pick. One part.

sheet-36.description: Sheet 36 continues the Garwood industrial strip southward at 50 feet to an inch, turned so that north is to the right of the page. Willow Avenue and South Avenue run down the left side, crossed by West about a third of the way down and by Center at the foot of the sheet. Between them and between Willow Avenue and the edge the blocks are cut into narrow lots, with a row of brick stores at the lower left along Center and Willow Avenue, a loft building and a few frame dwellings. The centre of the sheet is occupied by factories: a vacant steel-frame building, the Zobell Elec. Motor Co., the Armor Bronze Co. making statuary, and, much larger, the plant of the United States Aluminum Corp'n for aluminum castings, a steel-framed works covering most of the block lower down and surrounded by its own water pipe and fence line. To the right of these lies the wide railroad corridor with its tracks and sidings. Beyond it is the Garwood Bronze & Foundry Co. foundry, shown as owned by that company and leased to the Federal Foundry Co., with a smaller foundry building below it. Maple is lettered at the top right as not open, North Avenue forms the right edge, and Walnut Street enters it from the right near the lower corner. Sheet 36 repeats the Esda Mfg. Co. building at the top, shared with sheet 35, and sheet 37 begins below Center.
notes: Maple is lettered Not Open on this sheet.

West is West Street and Center is Center Street in OpenStreetMap; the modern node where Center Street, North Avenue and Walnut Street meet lies about 50 m north of where this sheet draws Center Street meeting North Avenue, so that junction was not used.
The drawn railroad lies 10 to 17 m from the Raritan Valley Line in OpenStreetMap; no rail crossing was used.
50 ft. Willow Av to North Av, West to Center (Aluminum Corp, Armor Bronze, Federal Foundry); turned. One part.

sheet-37.description: Sheet 37 shows the middle of the Garwood factory strip at 50 feet to an inch, turned so that north is to the right. Center crosses the top of the sheet and East crosses it about two thirds of the way down, with Willow Avenue and South Avenue running along the left. On the left, between Center and East, the blocks hold frame dwellings and a few shops; a row of brick stores with a bank, a drug store, the Post Office and the Fire Department and Boro Hall stands on the south side of Center, with a fire alarm box at the corner. In the middle of the sheet, beside South Avenue, is a large complex of brick and frame works marked as the foundry and machine shop of the radiator and boiler division of the Thatcher Co., spread over several blocks, with a new machine shop, a core room and a sand bin, and the Pioneer Products Co. above it. Across the railroad corridor, at the right, stand the New Jersey Foundry and Machine Co., the Diamond Expansion Bolt Division of Henry B. Newhall Corp., a perforating company making perforated metal products and screens, a welding department, machine shop, boiler house and a gymnasium and dance hall with bowling alleys. North Avenue runs down the right edge with Cedar Street entering it from the right. A long cluster of railroad tracks and sidings runs from top to bottom through the middle right.
notes: Center is Center Street, East is East Street and Cedar is Cedar Street in OpenStreetMap.
The drawn railroad lies about 19 m from the Raritan Valley Line in OpenStreetMap; no rail crossing was used.
The modern Cedar Street and North Avenue node lies about 4 m from the junction as drawn and was not used.
50 ft. Willow Av to North Av, Center to East (Thatcher foundry, post office, borough hall); turned. One part.

sheet-38.description: Sheet 38 covers the southern part of the Garwood industrial strip at 50 feet to an inch, turned so that north is to the right of the page. Willow Avenue and South Avenue run down the left, crossed by Oak Street South a little above the middle and by New at the foot of the sheet. The blocks between and beside them are divided into very narrow lots that are almost entirely vacant, with only a few frame houses near blocks 4 and 55. A large blank area between South Avenue and the railroad is the unbuilt block 22, and a compass rose and scale bar fall in the white ground. The upper centre of the sheet is the storage warehouse of The Thatcher Company, with its machine shop, repeated from sheet 37. A broad band of railroad tracks and sidings crosses the sheet from top to bottom. On the right, between the tracks and North Avenue, stand the long brick factory buildings of the Aeolian Co., with the Votey Organ Co. noted as its subsidiary, makers of pianos, pianolas, organs and vocalions, with a mutual risk notice, a reservoir, a water tower, a coal house and boiler house, and a spur from the tracks. North Avenue forms the right edge, with Oak Street North entering it from the right near the middle. The sheet number 38 is printed at the upper left and right.
notes: Oak Street South is Oak Street, New is New Street and Oak Street North is North Oak Street in OpenStreetMap.
The drawn railroad lies about 11 m from the Raritan Valley Line in OpenStreetMap; no rail crossing was used.
The junction of North Avenue and Oak Street North was left out: the modern node lies about 8 m from the junction as drawn.
50 ft. Willow Av to North Av, Oak St S to New (Aeolian organ works); turned. One part.

sheet-39.description: Sheet 39 is the last of the Garwood industrial strip, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the right. New crosses the top of the sheet, with Willow Avenue and South Avenue running down the left. The blocks below New are narrow vacant lots with one frame dwelling at the top. The left and lower parts of the sheet are cut off by the Cranford Township line, a dash-dot line running diagonally down to the right, and the ground beyond it is lettered See Map of Cranford. South Avenue bends along this line, and a dashed Elsie Street meets it with a water pipe; Willow Avenue is cut off by the same boundary. A few frame buildings stand on the Garwood side of the line near Elsie Street. The railroad tracks and sidings continue down the middle right of the sheet. At the right, beside North Avenue, are the warehouses, boiler house and storage buildings of the Anchor Post Fence Co., makers of fences and wrought iron work, with a freight house, and a vacant lot lower down. Winslow Place and Anchor Place enter North Avenue from the right, and Lincoln Avenue runs along the Borough Line at the lower right, drawn 50 feet wide. A large Westfield N.J. stamp, the word Garwood and the sheet number 39 occupy the upper right, and a library map division stamp falls in the blank centre.
notes: New is New Street in OpenStreetMap; Elsie Street is Elise Street there.
The sheet is anchored on one junction (New with Willow Avenue) at the atlas scale; New with South Avenue agrees with it to 1 m.
The right-hand part of North Avenue bends and was not used for control.
50 ft. New St to the Cranford line (Anchor Post Fence Co); turned; anchored on New / Willow. One part.

sheet-40-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 40 is the lower and larger part of the sheet, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north near the top of the page. It shows the eastern edge of Garwood, below a heavy line that sets off part 2. The avenues 5th, 4th, 3rd and 2nd run across the page at regular intervals, crossed at the left by Oak Street North, with North Avenue East along the foot. The blocks between are cut into narrow lots and are well built up with frame dwellings, with numerous outbuildings, particularly near 2nd and 3rd Avenues. Hydrants, fire alarm boxes and water pipes are shown in each avenue, and the blocks are numbered 31, 38, 40, 41, 50 and others.
