At the lower right Anchor Place runs diagonally up from North Avenue East between two rows of dwellings, with Winslow Place and a small group of lots beside it, and the boundary line of Cranford Township cuts across the right half of the part diagonally; the ground beyond it is blank and lettered See Map of Cranford. A garage and other buildings stand near Lincoln Avenue at the lower right. A library map division stamp and the numbers of the adjoining sheets and blocks are printed along the margins.
notes: Oak Street North is Oak Street north of 2nd Avenue and North Oak Street south of it in OpenStreetMap; North Avenue East is North Avenue there.

Placed on four junctions along Oak Street North, one at Anchor Place and North Avenue and a hand-picked junction of 2nd Avenue and Anchor Place; the points are not well spread across the right of the part.
Sheet numbers printed at the margins refer to adjoining sheets.

100 ft. Two parts divided by a heavy bent line: part 1 lower (2nd to 5th Avs, Oak St N, Anchor Pl, North Av E; one hand pick); part 2 upper (Hickory Av, East, Center, Columbus Av, Lexington Av; helmert on three Hickory Av junctions).

sheet-40-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 40 is the upper part, behind the heavy line that crosses the sheet from the left edge to the right edge in a bend, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north near the top of the page. It shows the south side of Hickory Avenue from the Westfield line at the left to Lexington Avenue at the upper right. Hickory Avenue runs along the top and the narrow blocks 91 and 92 front it, with a few frame dwellings, a coop and a shed, divided into narrow lots; East runs down the page from Hickory Avenue into the blank block 94. Center and Columbus Avenue enter at the upper left, crossing the Garwood Borough and Westfield Township line, with blocks 380 and 15 and a few buildings on the Westfield side. Wood Avenue is lettered on a diagonal street at the middle right, with block 96 divided into long lots and a few frame dwellings. Lexington Avenue appears as a 50 foot street along the Borough Line at the top right. Most of the area is blank, lettered See Map of Cranford, and carries a Westfield N.J. stamp and the word Garwood with block numbers 94 and 95. A compass rose and the sheet number 40 stand at the right.
notes: East is East Street and Center is Center Street in OpenStreetMap; Wood Avenue is not in OpenStreetMap.
Placed by three junctions along Hickory Avenue (with East, Center and Lexington Avenue), so all control lies on one street; low confidence in the placement across the page.

100 ft. Two parts divided by a heavy bent line: part 1 lower (2nd to 5th Avs, Oak St N, Anchor Pl, North Av E; one hand pick); part 2 upper (Hickory Av, East, Center, Columbus Av, Lexington Av; helmert on three Hickory Av junctions).

sheet-41-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 41 covers the south-western corner of the Borough of Garwood and the adjoining edge of Westfield, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north close to the top of the page. The regular Garwood grid fills the upper and right parts of the sheet: Willow, Myrtle, Spruce, Locust, Beech, Pine, Hazel and Hemlock Avenues run across the page, crossed by Maple Avenue, West Street and Center Street, with Hickory Street lettered at the right edge. The blocks are divided into many narrow 25 ft lots, a large share of them still vacant, with frame dwellings and garages scattered along Willow, Myrtle and Spruce Avenues and a fuller row on Locust Avenue east of West Street. St. Mark's Church (Episcopal) stands on Center Street between Locust and Beech Avenues, and a fire alarm box is marked on Center Street. At the left the curving line of East Grove Street enters from Westfield, and Elizabeth Avenue and Columbus Avenue run diagonally across the lower left, with Sycamore lettered where it meets Columbus Avenue. The Garwood Borough and Westfield Township line follows a dash-dot line along the north-east side of Columbus Avenue; a row of houses on Columbus Avenue is marked as drawn from plans. In the lower right corner the blocks between Hemlock Avenue and Center Street (block 381) are large and unbuilt, and the Clark Township line and the railroad appear at the bottom edge. A heavy line from the lower left sets off part 2, a 400 ft to an inch inset of the area along Rahway Avenue and Lamberts Mill Road.
notes: St. Mark's Church (Episcopal) on Center Street.
The Garwood and Westfield line runs along Columbus Avenue.
Sycamore is Sycamore Street today; Center is Center Street; West is West Street.

Garwood south-west corner (Willow to Hemlock Av, Maple to Center; Columbus Av on the Westfield line). Two parts: part 1 main at 100 ft; part 2 lower left behind a heavy line at 400 ft to an inch (Rahway Av, Lamberts Mill Rd, brook, Lehigh Valley RR; blocks 470-472, 520, 521), not placed.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset at 400 ft to an inch: Rahway Avenue, Lamberts Mill Road and the brook south of Westfield (open land with small streets (McKinley, Baltimore, Seward, Gardner) too small to detect at 400 ft; no junction identified with confidence; needs anchored placement on Lamberts Mill Road / Rahway Avenue or the Lehigh Line crossing with px_per_ft about 0.98 and north_deg about 3).

sheet-42-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 42 covers the eastern half of Garwood's residential grid, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north close to the top of the page. Willow, Myrtle, Spruce, Locust, Beech, Pine, Hazel, Hemlock and Hickory Avenues run across the sheet, crossed by Center on the left edge, East in the middle and Oak Street South at the upper right; Brook is lettered between Willow and Myrtle Avenues. The blocks are cut into narrow lots of about 25 ft. The western blocks between Center and East are well built up with frame dwellings and garages, especially between Willow and Locust Avenues; the blocks south of Beech Avenue and east of East are still largely vacant. The Washington Public School, a brick building with steam heat and electric light, stands in block 19 between Locust and Beech Avenues, and the Garwood Presbyterian Chapel in block 14 between Spruce and Locust Avenues. A church stands at the corner of Center and Brook in block 6. Fire alarm boxes are marked along Center. In the lower right Lexington Avenue and Rankin Avenue run diagonally along the borough line, lettered Cranford Township and See Map of Cranford, and the blocks there are cut off at an angle. A heavy line at the right sets off part 2, an inset of the blocks along New Street, which on the ground lie just beyond the right edge of the main map between Willow and Spruce Avenues.
notes: Oak Street South is Oak Street in OpenStreetMap; Center is Center Street; East is East Street.
Brook is not in OpenStreetMap.
Washington Public School and Garwood Presbyterian Chapel.
Center Street / Willow Avenue was rejected at 6.3 m.

100 ft. Garwood east (Willow to Hickory Av, Center to Oak St S; Washington Public School). Two parts: part 1 main; part 2 inset at right behind a heavy line (New St between Willow and Spruce Avs, blocks 56, 57, 60, 61), anchored on two New St junctions.

sheet-42-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 42 is an inset on the right side of the sheet, framed by a heavy line, showing the north-east corner of Garwood beyond the right edge of the main map. It is drawn at the same scale, 100 feet to an inch, and orientation as part 1. New runs down the middle of the inset, crossed by Willow Avenue at the top and Myrtle Avenue lower down, with Spruce Avenue at the bottom and Rankin Avenue cutting diagonally across the lower left corner along the borough line. West of New lie the eastern ends of blocks 56 and 57, east of it blocks 60 and 61, all divided into narrow lots. Building is sparse: frame dwellings on Willow Avenue in blocks 56 and 60 and a single dwelling in block 57. The right part of the inset, beyond a dash-dot borough line, is blank and lettered Cranford Township and See Map of Cranford. Sheet numbers 38, 39 and 42 printed in and beside the inset point to the adjoining sheets.
notes: Placed from two detected junctions on New Street (Willow and Myrtle Avenues), 284 ft apart, with the configured scale: anchored, low confidence.
New is New Street in OpenStreetMap.

100 ft. Garwood east (Willow to Hickory Av, Center to Oak St S; Washington Public School). Two parts: part 1 main; part 2 inset at right behind a heavy line (New St between Willow and Spruce Avs, blocks 56, 57, 60, 61), anchored on two New St junctions.
